title: Which of the following statements regarding alveoplasty procedures is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Simple alveoplasty utilizes a buccal flap to adequately expose the buccal bone.
omfs: Intraseptal alveoplasty does not utilize a buccal flap to expose the buccal bone.
midterm: A disadvantage of an intraseptal alveoplasty is that the ridge width is lessened.
column5: A simple alveoplasty works well to contour irregularities of the buccal bone.
column6: Alveoplasty procedures must be utilized to eliminate all bony undercuts.

title: Whenever a tuberosity reduction is performed, bone and soft tissue must both be removed.
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: This statement is TRUE.
omfs: This statement is FALSE.

title: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of inflamed fibrous hyperplastic soft tissue such as an epulis is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When a small, well-localized area of fibrous hyperplasia is excised, simple closure of the mucosal wound margins should be performed.
omfs: When a large area of inflammatory fibrous hyperplasia is excised, primary closure of mucosal tissues would result in reduction or elimination of the labial vestibule.
midterm: When a large area of inflammatory fibrous hyperplasia is excised, supraperiosteal removal followed by suturing of the mucosal edge to the periosteum at the depth of the vestibule should be performed to preserve the labial vestibule.
column5: The amount of tissue excised determines the depth of the labial vestibule.  Suture technique does not have any effect on this depth.

title: Which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) about frenectomy procedures is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: This procedure may be done with a laser.
omfs: Suture techniques can influence the final result.
midterm: The Z-plasty technique involves additional incisions after the frenum is excised with the intent of decreasing loss of vestibular depth.
column5: Frenectomy may be useful in reducing denture displacement.
column6: None of the statements (A, B, C, D) are FALSE. All of the statements (A, B, C, D) are TRUE.

title: Which of the following statements regarding the Transpositional Flap Vestibuloplasty, also known as the Lip Switch Procedure, is NOT TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Bone height of at least 5 mm is required for this procedure to be useful.
omfs: If adequate lingual vestibular depth is not present, this procedure will not be useful.
midterm: This procedure involves a supra-periosteal dissection along the anterior aspect of the mandible.
column5: The exposed labial tissue heals by secondary intention.
column6: Disadvantages of the procedure include possible relapse and vestibular scarring.

title: Which of the following statements regarding Immediate Denture techniques for a full upper denture is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Posterior teeth should be extracted initially with adequate time allowed for healing prior to denture fabrication.
omfs: Immediate Dentures allow patients to maintain their anterior teeth for esthetic and psychological benefits until their dentures are inserted.
midterm: Final ridge form is simulated by removing the teeth to be extracted on the final models prior to denture fabrication.
column5: This technique can utilize either digital or conventional analog impressions.
column6: Dentures should be inserted and adjusted when the anterior teeth are removed and then left out for at least one week to allow for healing.

title: Which of the conclusions to the following sentence are FALSE: The purpose of this course is to teach dental students about Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery so that as general practitioners, you can:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: understand what oral surgical treatments are available for your patients.
omfs: understand the risks and benefits of oral surgical procedures that your patients may undergo.
midterm: understand the post-operative course for your patients following various oral surgical procedures.
column5: perform any oral surgical procedure that your patients may need.
column6: talk to your patients about oral surgical procedures.

title: Which of the following statements about obtaining a medical history is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Asking questions that seem redundant may yield different information.
omfs: Medical history should be updated for all patients once a year.
midterm: Asking age-appropriate questions to children and adolescents when they are separated from their parent/guardian may yield important information that was not obtained from the parent/guardian.
column5: Patients’ health literacy must be considered when interpreting answers.
column6: Patients may realize secondary gain by misinforming the history taker.

title: It’s 3 months from now and (hopefully) you are seeing your first TDH clinic patient.  They get impatient waiting for the elevator so they take the stairs.  They climb one flight, stopping along the way.  They continue to clinic on the elevator. You question them and learn that they have coronary artery disease with stents placed 3 months prior.  They also have poorly controlled diabetes. Which ASA classification describes this patient:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: ASA I.
omfs: ASA II.
midterm: ASA III.
column5: ASA IV.
column6: ASA V.

title: Which of the following does NOT have an effect on a patient’s hemostasis status?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Type I diabetes.
omfs: Chemotherapy.
midterm: Use of NSAIDs such as ibuprofen.
column5: Liver disease.
column6: Heparin given during renal dialysis.

title: Which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Target specific oral anticoagulants should always be discontinued prior to performing dental extractions.
omfs: Patients on antiplatelet therapy such as baby aspirin (81 mg) and/or clopidogrel should always stop these medications prior to undergoing dental extractions.
midterm: Warfarin should always be discontinued 3 days prior to dental extractions.
column5: Patients on heparin for dialysis should always have their INR checked prior to undergoing extractions.
column6: None of the statements (A, B, C, D) are TRUE. All of the statements (A, B, C, D) are FALSE.

title: Which of these statements regarding platelets is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Patients may have bleeding issues after extractions due to quantitative problems with their platelets.
omfs: Patients may have bleeding issues after extractions due to qualitative problems with their platelets.
midterm: Normal platelet count ranges from 150,000 to 450,000 platelets per microliter of blood. If a patient has fewer than 100,000 platelets per microliter, platelet transfusions should be given before extractions or abnormal bleeding will occur.
column5: Timing of surgical procedures for patients with a history of qualitative platelet issues may be critical as this condition is often episodic.
column6: Administration of DDAVP and/or corticosteroids may increase platelet levels.

title: The following management techniques are all recommended when treating diabetics, EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Administration of prophylactic antibiotics before all surgical procedures.
omfs: Preference for patients to have mild to moderate hyperglycemia rather than hypoglycemia during surgical procedures.
midterm: Delay elective surgical procedures until poorly controlled diabetic patients are better controlled.
column5: Patients’ insulin doses should be adjusted based on pre-op intake and anticipated post-op intake.
column6: Patients should be observed for signs of hypoglycemia during procedures.  These signs may include hypotension, hunger, drowsiness, nausea, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and mood change.

title: Which of the following statements pertaining to HIV+ patients is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: About 1/5 of HIV+ patients have a decreased platelet count which puts them at significant risk of bleeding during and/or after oral surgical procedures.
omfs: Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to all HIV+ patients prior to oral surgical procedures because they have an increased risk of developing post-operative infections.
midterm: Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to HIV+ patients with a CD4+ T cell count <700 prior to oral surgical procedures.
column5: Prophylactic antibiotics should be administered to HIV+ patients with a neutrophil count <500 prior to oral surgical procedures.
column6: A decision to administer prophylactic antibiotics to HIV+ patients prior to oral surgical procedures should be based solely on their HIV status and should not take into account any other conditions that they may have.

title: All of the following are potential risks or problems with unnecessary prescribing of antibiotics, EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Adverse reactions.
omfs: Allergic reactions.
midterm: Gastrointestinal issues.
column5: Development of resistant organisms.
column6: Cost.
column7: All of these are potential risks or problems.

title: Which of the following statements regarding the management of patients who are having or have had chemotherapy or radiation therapy is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Patients who are having or have had chemotherapy or radiation therapy all have the same risk for developing infections following oral surgical procedures.
omfs: Patients who have had radiation treatment are more prone to infections including ORN (osteoradionecrosis) following oral surgical procedures in the maxilla than the mandible.
midterm: Patients with a history of chemotherapy will generally exhibit a reduction or elimination of their risk for infection following oral surgical procedures after the chemotherapy is stopped and their hematopoietic system has been allowed to recover.
column5: The risk of infection following oral surgical procedures in patients who have had radiation therapy is not related to the dose or field of the radiation.
column6: In patients undergoing pre-irradiation extractions, the teeth should be removed as simply as possible without reduction of sharp areas and without achieving primary soft tissue closure.

title: Which of the following statements made by an asthmatic patient may make you think that they are at increased risk of having an “asthma attack” during treatment?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: “The frequency of my asthma attacks has decreased since I was a child.”
omfs: “I have never needed to go to the Emergency Room for my asthma.”
midterm: “My asthma attacks only occur when I exercise.”
column5: “I have only been intubated for my asthma twice in the past year.”
column6: None of these statements would make you think that your patient is at increased risk of having an “asthma attack”.

title: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: It may be problematic if a patient’s blood pressure and/or heart rate is significantly higher or lower than their baseline values.
omfs: Patients with congestive heart failure should not be placed in the supine position.
midterm: Epinephrine may increase a patient’s heart rate and/or blood pressure.
column5: If a patient tells you that they had cardiac stents placed, you know that they had a myocardial infarction.
column6: Patients with atrial fibrillation are often anticoagulated.

title: What is the most important piece of information to gather during your patient assessment directly from your patient?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Chief complaint/concern.
omfs: Extraoral Exam.
midterm: Intraoral Exam.
column5: Panoramic Radiograph.
column6: Periapical Radiographs.

title: In which of the following scenarios is extraction NOT indicated?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Tooth 9 which is class I mobile due to traumatic occlusion.
omfs: Tooth 19 retained root tips with PAR increased from 6 months prior.
midterm: Tooth 29 with pulpal necrosis and the patient refuses endodontic treatment.
column5: Tooth 6 with class III+ mobility and chronic severe localized periodontal disease.
column6: Tooth 32 with associated operculum and pericoronitis.

title: In which of the following patient scenarios would an extraction be possibly contraindicated?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: 72-year-old male with a recent history of stage IV oropharyngeal cancer who had head and neck radiation therapy in the area of the maxilla and mandible 10 months ago.
omfs: 28-year-old female with pericoronitis of tooth 17 who is 8 weeks pregnant (i.e. in her first trimester).
midterm: 56-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease and now controlled hypertension on enalapril and aspirin.
column5: A & C.
column6: A & B.

title: Please assess this scenario and determine whether this would be a complicated or uncomplicated tooth extraction: 33-year-old female, otherwise healthy, presents with a partial bony impacted tooth 16. There is a distal operculum with some localized irritation and one of the mesial cusps is visible.
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Complicated.
omfs: Uncomplicated.

title: Please assess this scenario and determine whether this would be a complicated or uncomplicated tooth extraction: 62-year-old male, with controlled type II diabetes, presents with severe pain on tooth 24. It has deep periodontal pocketing with bleeding on probing and has class III mobility.
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Complicated.
omfs: Uncomplicated.

title: Please assess this scenario and determine whether this would be a complicated or uncomplicated tooth extraction: 87-year-old male who has a cardiac pacemaker and is on warfarin. His INR is 2.3. He presents with asymptomatic but grossly carious tooth 30. There is no crown structure left and the tooth was previously endodontically treated. It is deemed nonrestorable and indicated for extraction.
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Complicated.
omfs: Uncomplicated.

title: When extracting anterior maxillary or anterior mandibular incisors, what directional forces do you put on the tooth when using your forceps to deliver the tooth?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Buccal.
omfs: Apical.
midterm: Rotational.
column5: A & B.
column6: A & C

title: On which of the following teeth is it CONTRAINDICATED to use a cowhorn forceps during extraction?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Tooth 18.
omfs: Tooth 19.
midterm: Tooth 30.
column5: Tooth 31.
column6: Tooth 32.

title: You have completed an extraction of tooth 19 on a 47-year-old patient. You notice that the buccal cortical plate has an area of sharpness. Which of the following instruments should you use to smoothen the sharp area?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Bone file.
omfs: Rongeur.
midterm: Currette.
column5: A&B.
column6: A&C.

Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Weider.
omfs: Seldin.
midterm: Minnesota.
column5: A&B.
column6: A&C.

title: You have a 64-year-old male who has presented for extraction of tooth 11. Which of the following is the appropriate position to place the patient in during surgery?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Seated with mandible parallel to the ground.
omfs: Semi-supine with chair elevated such that the operator’s elbows are straight instead of at 90 degrees to the patient to enable reaching.
midterm: Semi-supine or supine with elbows at 90 degrees to enable maximum mobility.
column5: Trendelenberg to enable full direct visualization of the surgical site.
column6: Pronated for patient comfort.

title: You extracted tooth 4 on a 55-year-old with no significant medical history. He has had multiple extractions in the past without any complication. You call him that evening to check and see how he’s doing. He reports that he’s still bleeding from the surgical site, but it’s not profuse and asks you what he should do. You remember that during your surgery, it was an uncomplicated atraumatic extraction with minimal bleeding and you obtained good hemostasis at the end before discharging him. What should you do?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Tell him to go to the nearest hospital Emergency Department immediately.
omfs: Tell him to go see his physician to get a coagulation panel to find out whether he has any underlying blood dyscrasias.
midterm: Find out whether he is using his gauze packs properly and instruct him to place gauze with firm pressure at the site for 45-60 minutes.
column5: Assume that he has been following all post-operative instructions properly and instruct him to immediately place a black tea bag at the site for 1.5 hours to help with hemostasis.
column6: Tell him to begin rinsing with 100% hydrogen peroxide mouth rinse to constrict the vasculature at the extraction site to aid in hemostasis.

title: You have a 36-year-old female in your chair and have attempted to extract tooth 14. Unfortunately, the crown fractured off and you must convert to a surgical extraction with a flap for access. Which of the following is true?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: You should create a split thickness mucoperiosteal flap that can be sulcular or have one or two releasing incisions if necessary.
omfs: You should create a flap where the free margin is broader than the base to enable good blood supply for healing.
midterm: You should create a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap that includes reflection of periosteum which when sutured back will aid in bony healing.
column5: You should create a split thickness mucoperiosteal flap that includes reflection of periosteum which when sutured back will aid in bony healing.
column6: You should create a 6-cornered flap to optimize visibility and access to the surgical site.

title: Which of the following flaps is the most appropriate flap to make given the clinical scenario?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: You are extracting tooth 32. You create a flap with a lingual releasing incision.
omfs: You are extracting tooth 20. You create a flap with a releasing incision that extends deep into the vestibule right between teeth 20, 21.
midterm: You are extracting tooth 11. You create a semilunar flap.
column5: You are extracting tooth 19. You create a sulcular flap with no releasing incisions.
column6: You are extracting tooth 15. You create a flap with a palatal releasing incision that extends beyond the vibrating line.

title: Which of the following flaps is the most appropriate flap to make given the clinical scenario?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: You are extracting tooth 9. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical release beginning directly on the facial aspect of tooth 9.
omfs: You are extracting tooth 5. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical releasing incision directly on the papilla between teeth 5, 6.
midterm: You are extracting tooth 3. You create a four-cornered flap with one vertical release crossing the free gingival margin at the line angle of tooth 2 and one vertical release directly across the papilla of tooth 4.
column5: You are extracting tooth 27. You create a three-cornered flap with your vertical release crossing the free gingival margin at the line angle of tooth 26.
column6: You are extracting tooth 23. You create a four-cornered flap with the free margin broader than the base.

title: When you are suturing, what angle should your suture needle enter mucosal tissue?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: 30 degrees.
omfs: 45 degrees.
midterm: 60 degrees.
column5: 90 degrees.
column6: 105 degrees.

title: You have a 44-year-old female with non-restorable tooth 31. You note that tooth 31 was previously endodontically treated and has a very unstable crown. You plan to approach this extraction surgically. What is the proper way to section this tooth?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Buccal-palatally, but stopping ¾ of the way to the palate.
omfs: Buccal-lingually, but stopping ¾ of the way towards the lingual.
midterm: Mesio-distally, but stopping ¾ of the way towards the distal.
column5: Buccal-lingually, going all the way through the tooth to the lingual cortex.
column6: Mesio-distally, going all the way through the tooth to the distal and stopping before hitting tooth 32.

title: Which of the following teeth extractions will likely require surgical sectioning during your procedure?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Tooth 19 with significant bone loss and class II mobility.
omfs: Tooth 9 with some carious decay, but crown is mostly intact. There is no periodontal bone loss.
midterm: Tooth 18 with bulbous widely separated roots and minimal crown structure left.
column5: Tooth 16 fully erupted with small conical roots and buccally malpositioned.
column6: Tooth 24 fully erupted with pulpal necrosis.
